fixes.explanation: David says, "I sought the LORD, and He answered me; He delivered me from all my fears." Notice that the word is all. He doesn't say some of them or the small ones. That's David telling what happened when he sought the LORD.

David says, "The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear Him, and he delivers them." Encamps means pitching a camp, like a guard setting up right around you. I think that's about as close as protection gets.

David says, "Taste and see that the LORD is good; blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him!" Tasting is firsthand, not hearsay. You can't know what a fresh cookie is like by hearing about it, so I think David is inviting us to come find out for ourselves.
Hidden isn't the word David uses. He says, "Taste and see that the LORD is good…" Then he adds, "blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him!" The invitation is to taste and see that the LORD is good.
Hidden isn't what David says. He says, "He protects all his bones; not one of them will be broken." The verse is about protecting. Every one of those bones is kept from being broken.

David says, "Evil will slay the wicked, and the haters of the righteous will be condemned." That's a heavy line, and the word is condemned. Right after it, David says, "The LORD redeems His servants, and none who take refuge in Him will be condemned." (Psalm 34:22)

David ends with, "The LORD redeems His servants, and none who take refuge in Him will be condemned." Redeems is the word he closes on. The song ends with the LORD's servants and those who take refuge in Him.

Tests is a fair guess, baker, but David doesn't go there. He closes with, "The LORD redeems His servants, and none who take refuge in Him will be condemned." The last line of his song is about redeeming, and about no condemnation for those who take refuge in Him.
